parts.label: Rest-frame field energy U₀
parts.help: Neglect fringing, √A ≫ d; positive dimensions and ε₀.

parts.label: Longitudinal electric field Ex in S
parts.help: Boost parallel to the field; capacitor moves along +x in S. Other electric components vanish.

parts.label: Magnetic field magnitude in S
parts.help: Enter the result in the displayed unit, without a unit suffix.

parts.label: Moving-frame field energy
parts.help: γ = 1/√(1−β²) > 0; gap contracts longitudinally.

parts.label: Energy of each moving plate
parts.help: Each plate, not both; γ > 0, mp > 0, c > 0.

parts.label: Explain the apparent energy discrepancy
parts.help: The field and plates alone are not a closed static system; review why stressed supports carry the missing energy.

parts.label: Moving material-surface stress fxx
parts.help: Cauchy force per moving material-surface area, not a spatial stress-energy-tensor component. Positive stress means tension; γ = 1/√(1−β²).

parts.label: Right-minus-left force-release time interval
parts.help: Use x₀ for the positive rest-frame length Δx′. The right force disappears later; 0 < β < 1 and γ = 1/√(1−β²).

parts.label: Energy change during release
parts.help: Use V₀ for rest volume Δx′Δy′Δz′. Signed Cauchy stress fxx is negative for compression; work is then negative.

parts.label: Mass-equivalent density after release
parts.help: Rest energy density/c² is ρ₀; γ = 1/√(1−β²).

parts.label: Mass-equivalent density while stressed
parts.help: t₀xx = f₀xx, positive for tension and negative for compression; γ = 1/√(1−β²).

parts.label: Required rest-frame strut stress
parts.help: Two identical struts share the plate attraction; compressive stress is negative.

parts.label: Energy-equivalent mass of one moving strut
parts.help: γ = 1/√(1−β²); one strut, including its stress contribution. The strut area cancels.

parts.label: Total field, plate and strut energy
parts.help: Complete closed system; U₀ is rest field energy and γ = 1/√(1−β²). Includes both plates and both supports.
